task_instruction:
Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought:
I've pulled up your account, John. Here's what I can see on our side:

- **Line 555-123-2002** (your phone): status **Active** — not suspended, contract valid through 2026-12-31.
- **Data usage:** 8.7 GB of your 15 GB Premium Plan allowance this cycle (cycle ends 2025-02-28) — you haven't hit your data limit.
- **Bills:** Your most recent issued bill (B1002, $150.00, due 2025-02-19) is current — nothing is overdue, so no billing-related restriction is in place.
- **Roaming:** currently **disabled** on your line.

Since the account side looks clean, this is likely a device-side issue. One question to narrow it down:

**Are you currently located outside your normal home coverage area (traveling domestically or internationally)?** If so, the fact that roaming is disabled on your line would explain the data problems, and I can enable it for you at no cost. It would also help to know what you see in your status bar when the data stops working — specifically whether you have signal bars, whether the "Data Enabled" icon is showing, and whether you're on 5G/LTE/4G/3G.
That explains it. I can enable international roaming on your line right now at no cost — let me do that first.

Your status bar tells us exactly what's going on: the **airplane mode icon is on**, and there are no signal bars or data icons at all. That explains everything — airplane mode disconnects all wireless radios (cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth), so your phone can't connect to any French network to roam on.

The fix is simple: **turn Airplane Mode OFF.**

Please go to your phone's quick settings (swipe down from the top of the screen) and tap the airplane icon so it's no longer highlighted. If you'd rather, I can trigger the toggle on your device directly — just say the word.

While you were waiting, I went ahead and **enabled international roaming on your line (555-123-2002) at no cost**, since roaming was previously off and you're traveling outside your home network in France. With roaming enabled on our side plus Airplane Mode off on your device, you should connect to a local French network and get your data back.

One more thing to check once Airplane Mode is off:

**Make sure Data Roaming is turned ON in your phone's settings** (Settings → Network & Internet / Mobile Network → Roaming → Data Roaming). This is the device-side switch — separate from the account-level roaming I just enabled for you. Both need to be on for data to work abroad.

Please turn off Airplane Mode and let me know what your status bar shows after that — specifically whether you now have signal bars and a network type (5G/4G/LTE). If you're still having trouble, I'll keep troubleshooting with you.

Good progress — Airplane Mode is off and you now have **excellent signal on 5G with data enabled**. That means your line is connected and roaming on a French network, and the account-side roaming I enabled is working.

But I spotted the likely culprit for the "snail's pace" part of your problem: **the Data Saver icon is showing**, meaning Data Saver mode is ON.

Data Saver restricts background data usage and throttles data to reduce consumption. That's a very common reason data feels like it's crawling even with full bars and 5G.

**Please turn Data Saver OFF on your device:**
1. Open **Settings**
2. Go to **Network & Internet** → **Data Saver** (on some phones it's **Connections** → **Data usage** → **Data Saver**)
3. Tap the toggle to turn it **Off**

I don't have the ability to flip that switch from my end, so it needs to be done on your phone.

**While you're in there, please also confirm Data Roaming is ON at the device level:**
- **Settings** → **Network & Internet** → **Mobile network / SIMs** → **Roaming** → **Data roaming** → **ON**

This is the device-side switch that pairs with the account-level international roaming I enabled for you. Both need to be on for data to work here in France.

Once you've made both changes, please try loading a webpage or app and let me know:
- How the speed feels now
- Whether the Data Saver icon is gone from your status bar

If it's still slow after that, we'll dig into other possibilities such as VPN status or your network mode preference.

Good work getting Data Saver off — that should already help with the slowness.

Yes, please check the device-side Data Roaming setting. I enabled international roaming on your **account/line** from my side, but there's a separate switch on the phone itself, and both need to be on for data to work while you're in France.

**On Android:**
1. Open **Settings**
2. Tap **Network & Internet** (or **Connections** on Samsung)
3. Tap **Mobile network** (or **SIMs**)
4. Look for **Roaming** and make sure **Data roaming** is **ON**

**On iPhone:**
1. Open **Settings**
2. Tap **Cellular** (or **Mobile Data**)
3. Tap **Cellular Data Options**
4. Make sure **Data Roaming** is **ON** (toggle green)

I can't read that setting from my end, so I'll need you to confirm it.

That said, your status bar is a good sign: you're showing **excellent signal, 5G, and data enabled** while abroad, which generally means your phone has already attached to a French partner network — that usually wouldn't happen if device-side data roaming were fully blocking things. But it's worth verifying so we're not missing anything.

Please also **test the actual speed** now — try loading a webpage, refreshing an app, or streaming something briefly — and let me know how it performs compared to before. If it's still crawling, tell me and I'll walk you through a few more checks (VPN and network mode preference).

One quick heads-up for peace of mind while you're abroad: your line 555-123-2002 has used **8.7 GB of your 15 GB allowance** for the current cycle (ending 2025-02-28). Roaming doesn't change your plan's data allowance, so if you get close to 15 GB, data connectivity can be affected. Let me know if you'd like to discuss options before that happens.

Yes — please go ahead and run a speed test on your device. That's exactly the right next step, and it'll tell us whether you have a working data connection now and how fast it actually is.

Note that this is something you'll need to do **on your phone** — I can't run it remotely from my end and read the result. You can either use your phone's built-in speed test if it has one, or simply open a browser and go to a speed test site (like fast.com or speedtest.net), or download and run a speed test app.

All your settings look correct from what you've described:
- ✅ Airplane mode off
- ✅ Data Saver off
- ✅ Mobile data on
- ✅ Device-side data roaming on
- ✅ SIM active
- ✅ 5G with excellent signal
- ✅ Account-level international roaming enabled (done from my side)
- ✅ Line active, no suspension, 8.7 of 15 GB used

So in theory everything is in place for roaming data in France. The speed test will confirm whether it's actually working.

**When you run it, please tell me the download speed result** and I'll interpret it. Roughly speaking:
- **Excellent / Good** → you're all set, the issue is resolved
- **Fair / Poor / Very poor** → we keep troubleshooting
- **No connection** → we investigate further on the account side

Go ahead and run it, and let me know what you get. If it's still slow or not connecting, my next checks would be your **VPN status** (an active VPN can badly degrade speed abroad) and your **network mode preference**.

Excellent — 275 Mbps on Excellent is a great result, especially while roaming abroad. That's a solid connection that will handle browsing, apps, video streaming, and video calls without trouble.

To recap what resolved it:
1. **Airplane Mode** was ON — this was disconnecting all your wireless radios (cellular, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth), which is why you had no signal at all and data "stopped working completely."
2. **Data Saver** was ON — this was restricting and throttling your data, which explains the "snail's pace" when it did connect.
3. **International roaming** was OFF on your line — I enabled this from my side at no cost, since you're traveling in France.

A few notes for the rest of your trip:
- Your line **555-123-2002** has used **8.7 GB of your 15 GB** Premium Plan allowance for this cycle (ends **2025-02-28**). If you get close to 15 GB, data connectivity can be affected. If you need more, I can add up to 2 GB of refuel data at **$2.00/GB**, or we can look at other plan options — just let me know.
- Keep **Data Roaming** and **Mobile Data** on while abroad, and leave **Data Saver** off.
- If you're making calls, Wi-Fi Calling can help in areas with weaker cellular signal — happy to look at that if you're somewhere with spotty coverage.

Also, just so you're aware: your most recent bill (**B1002, $150.00**) is due **2025-02-19** and is currently issued but not yet paid. Nothing is overdue, but if you'd like to take care of it now I can send a payment request.

Glad we got you sorted out, and enjoy the rest of your time in France! Let me know if anything else comes up.
